current_bottleneck: Global sampler temperature does not fix the Gaussian likelihood model. Temp 0.75 recovers surface validity, daily-change KS, and persistent-undercoverage, but still fails conditionality, level occupancy, median bias, mean reversion, and pathwise jump realism. The bottleneck is the Gaussian transition family shape, not just sampling scale.
last_result_summary: 615a evaluated the 614a Gaussian likelihood checkpoint at sample temperatures 0.50 and 0.75. Temp 0.50 scored 3/11: surface passed, cov90 77.7%, conditional MAE 4.7%, persistent severe undercoverage 8.7%, daily KS 13/25, level KS 3/25, coin worst-cell 0.216, MR ratio 0.218, pathwise KS 0.846. Temp 0.75 scored 4/11: surface passed, cov90 87.2%, conditional MAE 4.7%, persistent severe undercoverage 4.8%, daily KS 15/25, level KS 2/25, median-bias cells 9/25, coin worst-cell 0.254, MR ratio 0.248, pathwise KS 0.801. Baseline temp 1.00 remains 4/11 but fails surface and has level KS 0/25.
next_step_recommendation: Close simple temperature calibration for 614a. Keep the likelihood-trained AR transition paradigm, but replace the Gaussian innovation family with a fixed-degree-of-freedom multivariate Student-t transition over the same empirical-score increments. This preserves exact conditional NLL and one shared state-panel model while giving the density family heavier tails without post-hoc stress calibration or separate IV/factor treatment.
current_best_note: 510a/392a remain the historical short-frame best learned IV laws at 8/11. On the 441-window broad frame, 510a, 596a, and 610a all score 5/11. 574a remains the best risk-manager joint stress product but is a composed deck, not a calibrated joint law. 610a is the cleanest native joint learned law so far because it generates IV and anchor factors through one shared AR transition model.
